text:
riley: Heads-up — ran into a bundler-specific bug when switching sample-app to rollup (Sapper/SvelteKit style) that only shows up on edge deployments. Node + vite dev are fine.

marta: what breaks exactly? build error or runtime?

riley: runtime. HTTP requests from the SDK end up with headers mutated across retries. Example observed: first request has Authorization header as expected, retry shows the header duplicated with comma separation. Logs show: 
```
[redwood] auth attempt failed 401
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY
Retrying...
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY, Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY
```

eric: similar symptom we saw before but with different bundler. Could be that the retry clones a Request object using new Request(oldReq) which doesn't deep-clone headers consistently across runtime shims.

zhen: which edge runtime? Cloudflare, Vercel Edge, Netlify?

riley: repro was on Netlify Edge Functions (V8 isolator). Rollup config uses @rollup/plugin-node-resolve + commonjs and a simple build target. I also tried a manual rollup + terser step; same thing.

marta: do you have a tiny repro repo/commands?

riley: yes — steps: 
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps -b rollup-edge-header-repro
2) cd sveltekit-rollup-edge
3) npm ci
4) REDWOOD_API_KEY=totallywrong npm run build:edge && npm run serve:edge
5) curl -v http://localhost:8888/api/prompt

The handler is tiny: 
```js
// src/routes/api/prompt.js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export async function post({ request }) {
  const out = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(await out.text());
}
```

eric: can you try forcing our retry to clone headers via new Headers(...) before creating a new Request? That fixed another case.

riley: did that locally by editing node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/retry.js — changed to: 
```js
const headers = new Headers(origReq.headers || {});
headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${apiKey}`);
const req2 = new Request(origReq, { headers });
```
It stops duplicating on my Netlify run. But we can't rely on people editing node_modules, obviously.

zhen: Packaging suspicion: maybe Rollup's commonjs plugin transforms our CJS bundle in a way that shares a Headers instance between retries because of inlined helper closure. Did you try switching to ESM-only import (pkg exports)?

riley: importing ESM entry still reproduced it. Oddly, when I import the CJS path directly (require from dist/cjs) the problem disappears.

marta: that hints at both packaging (exports map) and runtime differences. Also, we have lingering types issues for ESM consumers: TS server can't find overloads for createClient when import from ESM path in some bundlers. We need to ensure our package.json exports include a "types" entry for the ESM export.

eric: For immediate work: 
- add a tiny integration test that builds the sample with rollup and runs it on miniflare/netlify dev to assert header not duplicated (CI job).
- make our retry code create defensive clones of headers (new Headers(...)) so edge shims don't mutate shared state.

zhen: I'll open a PR to add a test matrix in CI (rollup + vite + edge runtimes) and a typescript compile step against a minimal ESM project to catch types resolution.

riley: I'll push the repro branch and add a README with exact rollup config + netlify.toml I used. Patch is trivial but we should run it across the matrix before publishing a patch.

marta: also add a note to the SDK CHANGELOG that the patch fixes header duplication on edge runtimes for rollback/patch transparency.

ci-bot: queued job: devex/rollup-edge-header-repro (#220) — running matrix: netlify-v8, cloudflare/workers-v8, wrangler-miniflare.

eric: quick thought — some bundlers inline global Headers polyfills which can be singletons. We should avoid mutating built-ins and prefer creating brand-new Headers objects. Also ensure we don't leak Request objects between retries.

zhen: agreed. I'll also search repo for places where we do new Request(oldReq) without an explicit headers clone.

riley: one more detail — when I build with rollup + the terser plugin (mangle=true) the failure becomes intermittent. Probably minified helper order changes how the runtime shares closures. This makes it tricky to reproduce reliably but supports the hypothesis that bundler transforms are part of the cause.

marta: good debugging. Let's track progress on the GH issue (sdk#439) and coordinate the CI job results here. Thanks all. :shipit:
